title: Running Totals of a List
statement: You get an array nums. Return a new array of the same length where position i holds nums[0] + nums[1] + … + nums[i], the total of everything up to and including index i.

examples.why: The first entry is nums[0] itself, not 0.
One element: its running total is itself.

hints: Each answer is a sum over a prefix. How is the prefix ending at i related to the one ending at i − 1?
out[i] = out[i − 1] + nums[i]. You never need to add up more than two numbers per position.
Keep one running total while scanning, and write it out at each step.

explain.intuition:
The total up to i is just the total up to i − 1 plus one more number. So instead of re-adding the whole prefix for every position, carry the running total forward as you scan. It is the balance column on a bank statement: each line is the previous balance plus this transaction.

This array has a name, the prefix sum, and it is the building block for a whole family of problems: range totals, subarrays with a given sum, and 2D region sums.
steps: Set total = 0 and create an output array.
For each x in nums, add it to total.
Write total to the output at the same index.
pitfalls: Writing the total before adding the current number, which shifts everything by one and starts with 0.
Recomputing each prefix from scratch, which is O(n²).
With values up to a million and n up to 100 000, totals reach 10¹¹. In a language with 32-bit ints, use 64-bit.

solutions.title: Re-add every prefix
solutions.idea: For each i, sum nums[0..i] from scratch.

solutions.title: Carry the total forward
solutions.idea: Keep a running total and write it at each index.

followups: Do it in place, overwriting nums, with O(1) extra space.
